page: UpCloud CLOUDNATIVE-20xCPU-96GB is a Cloud Native server family instance configured with 20 vCPUs and 96.0 GB of RAM, running on the KVM hypervisor. The system is powered by an AMD EPYC 9575F processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture. This CPU operates at a clock speed of 2.0 GHz, featuring 20 physical cores with a single thread per core. The processor includes a cache hierarchy of 64 KB L1d, 0.5 MB L2, and 16 MB L3 cache, alongside advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512, AES cryptography, and SHA extensions.

In benchmark testing, the instance demonstrates strong single-core capabilities, with a stress-ng single-core CPU score of 3506.58, placing it in the top tier (top 10%). However, multi-core performance is moderate, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 58026.34, which falls into the average category (middle 50%). This variance is influenced by the shared CPU allocation model, which introduces resource sharing tradeoffs compared to dedicated instances. Additionally, the instance does not include local storage or GPU hardware, meaning storage must be attached externally.

Given its shared CPU allocation and high memory-to-vCPU density of 4.8 GB per core, this server offers a cost-effective profile for workloads requiring substantial memory and high single-threaded performance without continuous multi-core utilization. It is suited for general-purpose applications, web serving, memory-intensive development environments, and background processing tasks that can tolerate shared CPU capacity.
